title: setDispatcherHook does not settle pending mint-debt from the old dispatcher before swapping, stranding accrued debt
regression-risk: pre-existing (noted in prior CS-12 but not separately tracked as a code bug)
description:
`setDispatcherHook` replaces the configured dispatcher without first calling `_syncBudget()` or `_updatePool()`. If the OLD dispatcher has accrued mint-debt that has not yet been pulled, that mint-debt is effectively stranded — the NEW dispatcher does not know to pull from the old one, and no code path pulls from the old address after the pointer changes. No zero-address check either; owner can accidentally set `address(0)`, which `_syncBudget` tolerates (early return) but which silently disables all pull-based funding.

This is a code-level ordering bug distinct from the centralisation concern of 'owner can swap dispatchers' (which is out of scope for dedup). The bug is that even a well-intentioned owner swap loses funds unless the owner manually remembers to call `pullAndRefresh` first.
impact: Owner-triggered operational footgun: any dispatcher swap without a preceding manual `pullAndRefresh` strands pending mint-debt at the old dispatcher. Recovery requires re-pointing to the old dispatcher to pull, or an old-dispatcher recovery path (out of scope). Not a direct adversarial exploit — a mistake-amplifier.
proof:
1. Old dispatcher has accumulated 1000 phUSD of mint-debt.
2. Owner calls `setDispatcherHook(newHook)`.
3. `dispatcherHook` now points to newHook.
4. User action triggers `_syncBudget` → `newHook.pull()` returns 0 (new hook hasn't accrued anything).
5. 1000 phUSD at old dispatcher is orphaned from the staker's perspective.
suggested-fix: Call `_syncBudget()` at the start of `setDispatcherHook` so pending mint-debt on the OLD dispatcher is pulled before the pointer changes. Add a zero-address check (or explicitly document that zero-address disables pulls). Consider emitting an additional event or warning when the swap leaves non-zero mint-debt behind.
consolidation-note: No ES overlap. Standalone ordering bug; distinct from the centralisation concern (which is out of scope for dedup).
sanitizer-note: Borderline vs C4 'reckless admin mistakes' known-invalid. Kept because the finding describes a coding defect (missing `_syncBudget` in a setter that is conceptually required to finalise the existing dispatcher's state) — the fix is a one-line code change, not an operator-procedure recommendation. If the severity-classifier disagrees, demote to Centralisation/QA.
